observations: CaptureDisposable adds a disposable object to the scope list under a lock at lines 77-98; this method itself has no identity deduplication.
Dispose traverses the captured list in reverse at lines 120-137 and has no catch around each synchronous Dispose call, so a thrown exception stops this loop.
Dispose throws InvalidOperationException upon reaching an async-only object at lines 128-135.
BeginDispose marks the scope disposed before invoking customer disposal code at lines 199-229.
SingletonServiceCreatedFromInstanceIsNotDisposedWhenContainerIsDisposed at lines 1099-1112 asserts a supplied singleton remains undisposed.
ProviderDisposeThrowsWhenOnlyDisposeAsyncImplemented at lines 946-958 asserts a synchronous close error for an async-only transient.

contractDifference: The internal Java OwnedResources helper continues closing after an Exception and suppresses subsequent failures. The pinned DI scope synchronous Dispose loop is fail-fast. These must not be described as the same behavior.
limits: Static source inspection only; no upstream test was executed in this batch.
This DI scope is a selected ownership example, not the complete IDisposable contract or all runtime ownership semantics.
